content.title: 7 Editor Extensions That Will Change How You Code
content.text:
Your editor is where you spend most of your working day, so it makes sense to invest a little time in making it better. The right extensions can turn a plain text editor into a powerhouse that catches bugs, formats your code, and keeps you focused. Today we are looking at 7 editor extensions that will change how you code. Some of these you may have heard of, and some may be new to you, but all of them are worth installing.

1. Brackethound — Ever lost track of which closing bracket belongs to which opening one? Brackethound colours matching pairs so you can see the structure of your code at a glance. It sounds small, but once you have it you will wonder how you ever managed without it.

2. Tidyfmt — Tidyfmt formats your code every time you save. No more arguing about tabs versus spaces or where the braces go. It supports dozens of languages and picks up your project's configuration file automatically, so the whole team stays consistent.

3. Blamelight — Blamelight shows who changed each line and when, right inside the editor. Hover over a line and you get the commit message, the author, and a link to the pull request. It is a lifesaver when you are trying to understand legacy code.

4. Snipforge — Snipforge lets you build your own snippet library with placeholders and tab stops. Type a short prefix, hit tab, and a whole function skeleton appears. Great for boilerplate you write over and over.

5. Errorlantern — Errorlantern displays warnings and errors inline, right next to the offending code, instead of hiding them in a panel you have to scroll through. You will fix problems faster simply because you see them sooner.

6. Pathwhisper — Pathwhisper autocompletes file paths as you type import statements. It knows your project layout, so it suggests the right relative path and even fixes it if you move a file. Fewer typos, fewer broken imports.

7. Focusdim — Focusdim greys out everything except the block of code you are currently editing. It is surprisingly effective at keeping you in the zone when you are deep in a large file. Toggle it with a shortcut when you need to see the bigger picture again.

And that wraps up our list of 7 editor extensions that will change how you code. Each one tackles a different pain point, from formatting to focus, and they all play nicely together. Install a few, give them a week, and notice how much smoother your day feels. Which extension made the biggest difference for you? Drop a comment below and tell us about the ones we should have included.

notes: Low-effort listicle about editor extensions: every item is a one-line benefit any working developer already knows (bracket colouring, format-on-save, inline errors). A correct judge should see no new information and rate it low value.
